pr_title: Don't throw an exception when a BQ cursor job has no schema
pr_comments: @uranusjr do you have other concerns? Is my explanation of the difference between my own issue and my own solution ok?

issue_context.title: Creative use of BigQuery Hook Leads to Exception
issue_context.body:
### Apache Airflow Provider(s)

google

### Versions of Apache Airflow Providers

8.3.0

### Apache Airflow version

2.3.4

### Operating System

Debian

### Deployment

Docker-Compose

### Deployment details

_No response_

### What happened

When executing a query through a BigQuery Hook Cursor that does not have a schema, an exception is thrown.

### What you think should happen instead

If a cursor does not contain a schema, revert to a `self.description` of None, like before the update.

### How to reproduce

Execute an `UPDATE` sql statement using a cursor.

```
conn = bigquery_hook.get_conn()
cursor = conn.cursor()
cursor.execute(sql)
```

### Anything else

I'll be the first to admit that my users are slightly abusing cursors in BigQuery by running all statement types through them, but BigQuery doesn't care and lets you.

Ref: https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/22328

review_comments: The linked issue says defaulting to None. Any reason to prefer either None or empty list?

When I initially wrote the linked issue I thought the original behavior was `None`, but it was actually just that `self.description` was never set at all.

Now that it's a defined list, I thought it would be better to set it up empty target than None.
